newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TIGER WOODS ELIGIBLE FOR RYDER CUP POINTS THIS WEEK.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER WOODS ELIGIBLE FOR RYDER CUP POINTS THIS WEEK.

text.p: Tiger Woods, golf's most exciting prospect in many years, is eligible to start earning U.S. team Ryder Cup points beginning with this week's Texas Open.
The 20-year-old Woods did not officially join the PGA Tour until after winning last Sunday's Las Vegas Invitational, so his performance there did not give him any Ryder Cup points.

Woods would have earned 75 points at Las Vegas, where he won in only his fifth start since turning professional after claiming his third consecutive U.S. Amateur title. He also would have accrued Ryder Cup points for top-10 finishes at Quad Cities and the B.C. Open.
But the budding superstar has until next August to earn a spot on the U.S. team that will take on Cup holders Europe at Valderrama in Spain next September.
Even if Woods does not automatically clinch one of 10 automatic spots on the team, he will surely be prominently considered for one of Tom Kite's two captain's picks.

Woods, who was two strokes off the lead after the second round at the Texas Open Friday, was not even aware of his Ryder Cup status. Until last Sunday, he had been more concerned with earning his PGA Tour card, which he secured through the end of 1998 with his Las Vegas victory.

Neither of those topics seemed to interest the long-hitting phenom as much as his Thursday night dinner with Charlie Sifford, a trailblazer who helped open professional golf to blacks during the 1960s.
"Mr Sifford's an amazing gentleman," Woods said. "He had to put up with an awful lot to play the game he loved. I truly admire him.
"If not for the Charlie Sifford's of the world, I may not be playing out here, because of the rules the tour had."
